 Transportation FAA issues nationwide ground stop citing communication issues affecting ‘multiple’ air traffic control facilities
 Published Fri, Nov 13 2026 4:01 PM EST Updated 5 Min Ago Leslie Josephs @lesliejosephs WATCH LIVE Key Points The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday afternoon, disrupting hundreds of flights.
 The agency reported communication problems affecting "multiple" air traffic control centers.
 Nationwide ground stops are extremely rare, and the last was in January 2023 after a failure of a pilot communication system.
 watch now VIDEO 2:11 02:11 Transportation Sec. Duffy says ground stoppage is due to communication issues Closing Bell: Overtime The Federal Aviation Administration halted departing flights nationwide on Friday after reporting communication problems affecting "multiple" air traffic control centers.
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Friday at the White House that there was no indication that the issues were a threat to the United States.
 The issues were related to communications and radar problems, according to an internal message from Alaska Airlines , which was seen by CNBC.
 "The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers," the FAA said. Its technicians are investigating, the agency said.
 Airlines said flights in the air would continue.
 Travelers wait inside San Francisco International Airport in San Francisco, California on Nov. 13, 2026. Jeniece Heinz | CNBC A ground stop halts flights at their departure point. Departing traffic was halted until further notice, the agency said, disrupting hundreds of flights. 
 Disruptions tend to snowball if ground stops drag on as flight crews reach their maximum number of duty hours for a day.
 Nationwide ground stops are extremely rare. In January 2023, the FAA halted flights because of issues with a pilot alert system. Before that, traffic was halted nationwide after the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks.
 Passengers queue at the Southwest Airlines desk to speak with a representative at Eppley Airfield in Omaha, Neb., on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. Nikos Frazier | Omaha World-Herald | Lee Newspapers | Getty Images There were 11,000 flights scheduled to depart U.S. airports after 4 p.m. ET on Friday, according to flight-data firm Cirium.
 Inbound international flights will be managed on a case by case basis, the FAA said. 
 United Airlines said it "will work with our customers to get them to their destinations once this issue is resolved."
 — CNBC's Kevin Breuninger contributed to this article.
